gloss: the pathos of things; mono no aware

definitions.gloss: the pathos of things; sensitivity to transience
definitions.explanation: A classical aesthetic ideal: the quiet, moving sadness felt on sensing that beautiful things pass. Associated above all with Heian literature and with the reading of {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}.

examples.japanese: {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: I feel the pathos of things.

examples.japanese: ⟦{散|ち}る→散る：02075_chiru⟧⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}えた→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧。
examples.english: The falling cherry blossoms stirred a sense of the pathos of things in me.

examples.japanese: {本居宣長|もとおりのりなが}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{源氏物語|げんじものがたり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{本質|ほんしつ}→本質：04810_honshitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{説|と}いた→説く：14245_toku⟧。
examples.english: Motoori Norinaga argued that the essence of The Tale of Genji lies in mono no aware.

notes:
Often written without kanji as もの⟦の→の：09472_no⟧あはれ in classical texts and as もののあわれ in modern ones. The Edo scholar {本居宣長|もとおりのりなが} made the phrase the centre of his reading of Heian literature, and it has been treated as a defining Japanese aesthetic ever since.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧: to feel the pathos of things
- {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}る→知る：00458_shiru⟧: to be sensitive to the pathos of things
- {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{美|び}→美：28891_bi⟧: the beauty of transience

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{無常|むじょう}→無常：13422_mujou⟧: impermanence — the Buddhist doctrine behind the feeling, not the feeling itself
- ⟦{侘|わ}び→侘び：10655_wabi⟧{寂|さび}: wabi-sabi — beauty in simplicity and age, a related but distinct ideal
- ⟦{切|せつ}ない→切ない：06167_setsunai⟧: bittersweet, aching — the everyday adjective for a comparable emotion
